methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $80M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
CarbonCapture Inc. is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Adrian Corless that has raised $80M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine private and one public company in the Climate & Energy sector, including late-stage peers KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. The Stage-Progression method applies a 1.9x multiplier to the $80M total raised as a proxy baseline, yielding $152M. The Peer-Median method examines three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with a median valuation of $1.0B and a range spanning $700M to $3.0B, implying $1.0B for CarbonCapture. These methods produce substantially divergent signals, reflecting the wide variance in public and private Climate & Energy valuations.

Triangulation across the two methods yields a median implied valuation of $576M, with a low of $129M and a high of $1.1B. The wide range reflects genuine uncertainty in stage-appropriate multiples within a volatile, capital-intensive sector. The Peer-Median method's reliance on three Series C comparables introduces stage-selection risk; Stage-Progression's dependence on raised capital as a valuation proxy may not account for unit economics or capital efficiency. A Series B round pricing would benefit from clarity on revenue traction, cash burn, and path to Series C financing to narrow this range.
